notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates. It reorganizes the menus, so things have moved.

Home screen: the IP address, clocks and temperatures are behind a System button in the header (you can pin each one back in Settings, Look and feel, Home screen header). There is a Recent tab with your last 12 games. Console tabs can be hidden and reordered in Settings, Library, Console tabs. L and R switch tabs. A game copied into a ROM folder now shows up within about half a minute, without a restart.

Game page: the rows are in three groups. Cheats, patches and community packs are one row, Mods and cheats. A save state you picked shows on the Play row. Anything that deletes or overwrites asks for a second press.

Pause menu: Quick save, Save state and Load state are at the top. Quit, Reset and deletes start on Cancel.

Settings: twelve sections. WiFi is under Network, updates and the date are under System, sleep and battery are under Power and sleep, and overclocking is last as Overclocking and tuning. Controllers has a Controls page that lists what every button does.

Web page: the tabs are Files, Graphics, PC Games, Ports, Accounts, Network, Console, Contributions and Support, and the page fits a phone. Updates and admin access are on Console; logs are on Support.

Battery: Settings, Power and sleep has Battery limits, which keeps the CPU and GPU under clocks picked for your model while running from the battery. It is off unless you turn it on, on for new installs, and the console turns it on by itself after a power-off the battery could not carry. The high battery draw warning now averages over three minutes.

New installs start with a mild RAM speed and CPU undervolt for their model. Consoles already set up are not changed.

Sharing: the launcher asks once whether to share anonymous usage data (which games crash, which features get used). It is off until you say yes.

Not yet tried on a TV, on the two clean themes, or with every emulator's pause menu. Reports welcome.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
